title: Cyclic coexistence of three Lenia replicator kinds holds down to 96^2 and 128^2 (3 of 4 runs keep all kinds to t=800); the one loss is a kind dying at founding (t<50), so no domain-size threshold for coexistence appears in 96-160^2
summary: world.py and runr.py of 20261025T2349-c26-rps-lenia (cyclic mode, PRATE 1, same parameters) at DOMAIN 96 and 128, seeds 1 and 2, t=0-800 (data/). 128^2: all three kinds persist on both seeds at 9-18 cells each with fluctuating counts (seed 1 final 11/14/14, seed 2 17/12/9). 96^2: seed 2 keeps all three at 5-12 cells each to t=800; seed 1 loses kind 0 before t=50, while the three planted founders still overlap (the placement rule cannot separate three founders in a 96 px domain), and the other two kinds then persist (16 and 10 cells). So the queue's prediction (cyclic coexistence only above a critical domain size) is not seen between 96^2 and 160^2 in this world; with 6-12 cells per kind at 96^2 the domain is already close to the minimum that holds three kinds at all.

finding.operator: cyclic predation between three Lenia replicator kinds
finding.control: domain size 96 and 128 vs the parent's 160, same parameters, seeds 1 and 2
finding.result: 128^2: 3/3 kinds to t=800 on 2/2 seeds; 96^2: 3/3 kinds on seed 2, kind 0 lost at founding (t<50) on seed 1

limits: Two seeds per size, 800 t, one predation rate; founders overlap at small sizes, so early losses reflect planting; no larger domains here (the parent ran 160^2).
